# Adjudication Task — Chapter 203

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃203화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|나는 눈앞에 뜬 시스템 메시지를 읽어 내려갔다.
  6|
  7|기절하듯 잠드느라 미처 확인하지 못한 퀘스트 보상에 관한 메시지였다.
  8|
  9|
 10|
 11|- 퀘스트, [일보 후퇴]를 성공적으로 완료했습니다!
 12|
 13|- 대량의 경험치를 얻었습니다!
 14|
 15|- 레벨 업!
 16|
 17|- 레벨 업!
 18|
 19|- 보너스 포인트 20을 획득했습니다!
 20|
 21|
 22|
 23|‘엄청 후하네.’
 24|
 25|레벨 업 두 번에 보너스 포인트까지 얻었으니 퀘스트 한 번으로 4레벨 업 정도의 효과를 본 셈이다.
 26|
 27|아마도 상대가 상대인지라 생각 이상으로 큰 보상을 받은 듯싶었다.
 28|
 29|‘창 닫기.’
 30|
 31|스스슥.
 32|
 33|반투명한 홀로그램 창이 사라지자 나를 향해 다가오는 적천강의 모습이 보였다.
 34|
 35|그의 손에는 미리 챙겨 온 행낭이 들려 있었다.
 36|
 37|“정신이 들었느냐?”
 38|
 39|“아, 예. 막 깼습니다.”
 40|
 41|“몸은 좀 괜찮고?”
 42|
 43|“가뿐합니다.”
 44|
 45|나를 위아래로 훑어본 적천강이 고개를 끄덕였다.
 46|
 47|“젊은 놈이라 그런지 기력도 금방 회복되는군. 곧바로 다음으로 넘어가도 되겠어.”
 48|
 49|“아, 다음이요. 그거 좋죠.”
 50|
 51|“그럴 줄 알았다. 노부가 네 녀석에게 딱 맞는 걸 준비해 뒀거든. 어디 보자…….”
 52|
 53|“저기, 노야.”
 54|
 55|“응?”
 56|
 57|“그, 다 좋은데요.”
 58|
 59|적천강을 향해 어색하게 웃으며 말을 이었다.
 60|
 61|“시작하기 전에 점혈(點穴) 좀 풀어 주시면 안 될까요.”
 62|
 63|말 그대로다.
 64|
 65|어떻게 된 일인지는 모르겠지만 처음 눈을 떴을 때부터 전신이 뻣뻣이 굳어 있는 상태였다.
 66|
 67|내가 잠든 사이 적천강이 마혈(痲穴)을 점한 것이다.
 68|
 69|지금 상태로 할 수 있는 것이라고는 소리 내어 말하는 것이 고작이었다.
 70|
 71|“물론 좋은 뜻으로 하신 거겠지만 슬슬 다음 수련도 해야 하니까…… 헤헤.”
 72|
 73|“아, 해야지. 수련.”
 74|
 75|적천강이 행낭을 뒤적거리며 덧붙였다.
 76|
 77|“이게 다음 수련이다.”
 78|
 79|“점혈 당하는 게 수련이라고요?”
 80|
 81|아니면 점혈을 푸는 게 수련인가?
 82|
 83|내가 헷갈려 하던 그때, 적천강이 행낭에서 뭔가를 꺼내 들었다.
 84|
 85|“여기 있었군. 맨 밑에 박아 놓고 깜빡했어.”
 86|
 87|“……그건 밧줄 아닙니까?”
 88|
 89|“맞다.”
 90|
 91|튼튼해 보이는 동아줄을 어깨에 두른 적천강이 성큼성큼 다가와 나를 번쩍 들어 올렸다.
 92|
 93|“뭐, 뭐 하시게요?”
 94|
 95|“금방 알게 될 게다.”
 96|
 97|이어 그의 발걸음이 향한 곳은 커다란 바위였다.
 98|
 99|얼마나 오랫동안 그 자리에 있었는지 지면 깊숙이 박혀 있었고, 성인 장정 여럿이 두 팔을 벌려도 못 안을 만큼 컸다.
100|
101|“음. 여기가 적당하겠군.”
102|
103|작게 중얼거린 적천강이 손날로 바위를 내리쳤다.
104|
105|서걱, 서걱.
106|
107|그의 손에 어린 붉은 강기가 천근거석을 치즈 케이크처럼 자르고 쪼갰다. 불과 몇 번의 손질 만에 바위는 별 다섯 개짜리 돌침대로 변해 있었다.
108|
109|“이 정도가 딱 적당하겠어.”
110|
111|“자, 잠깐만요. 설마 여기에 절 묶으려는 건 아니시죠?”
112|
113|“묶다니, 고정하려는 것이다.”
114|
115|“…….”
116|
117|똥이 아니라 대변이라고 하는 거랑 뭐가 다른 거야.
118|
119|아무튼 이쯤 되니 나도 슬슬 떨리기 시작했다.
120|
121|아니, 애초에 점혈부터가 수상하기 짝이 없었다. 아까부터 적천강이 뒤적거리고 있는 행낭의 존재도.
122|
123|‘설마 진짜 채찍이랑 가면이 나오는 건 아니겠지.’
124|
125|내가 동공 지진을 일으키는 동안 적천강은 밧줄로 내 몸을 바위에 고정시키기 시작했다.
126|
127|몸 곳곳에 밧줄을 두르고 단단히 묶은 그가 만족스럽게 웃었다.
128|
129|“이 정도면 어지간해서는 안 떨어지겠어.”
130|
131|“휴우.”
132|
133|“뭐냐, 그 안도의 한숨은?”
134|
135|“귀갑 매듭이 아니라서 안심했습니다.”
136|
137|“귀갑 매듭? 그게 무엇이냐?”
138|
139|“……일종의 포박술이죠.”
140|
141|“포박이라, 군문(軍門)에서 쓰는 것인가 보군.”
142|
143|“…….”
144|
145|주로 일본 애들이 많이 씁니다.
146|
147|‘뭐 어쨌든.’
148|
149|지금의 나는 대(大)자로 서 있는 것처럼 묶였다.
150|
151|양 손목과 발목, 그리고 가슴, 배, 다리. 정말 포박이 아니라 고정 그 자체가 목적인 듯싶었다.
152|
153|‘하긴 마혈을 짚었으니 꽁꽁 묶을 필요도 없겠지.’
154|
155|그런데 진짜 뭐 하려고 이러는 거지?
156|
157|눈동자만 뒤룩뒤룩 굴리던 그때, 적천강이 마침내 들고 있던 행낭을 풀어 젖혔다. 그리고 그와 동시에.
158|
159|화아악!
160|
161|“헉.”
162|
163|뭐라 형용할 수 없을 만한 향기가 뿜어져 나왔다.
164|
165|만성 비염 환자도 한 번에 완치될 것 같은 시원한 청량감이 코를 통해 전신 곳곳으로 퍼져 나간다.
166|
167|나는 눈을 크게 뜨고 행낭 안의 물건들을 바라봤다.
168|
169|“이건…….”
170|
171|가지런히 놓여 있는 세 개의 풀뿌리.
172|
173|불그스름한 빛을 띤 그것들을 집어 든 적천강이 자신의 손바닥에 올려놨다.
174|
175|“영약(靈藥)이다.”
176|
177|“헐, 이렇게 귀한 걸 어디서.”
178|
179|“창고를 뒤졌다. 온통 쓸모없는 것들만 가득 쌓아 놓는 바람에 더럽게 귀찮았지만.”
180|
181|산더미처럼 쌓인 비단이나 금은보화도 그의 눈에는 하등 쓸모없는 물건일 뿐이다.
182|
183|그러나 그는 뼛속까지 무인. 무공 증진에 도움 되는 영단, 혹은 비급이라면 이야기는 달라진다.
184|
185|“뭐, 사실 이 영단들도 썩 효과가 좋은 편은 아니다. 공력 증진으로 따지자면 오히려 백 년 하수오나 설삼이 훨씬 낫지.”
186|
187|“그런데 왜…….”
188|
189|“굳이 이걸 가져왔느냐고?”
190|
191|“예.”
192|
193|“오직 이것들로만 순수한 열양지기를 얻을 수 있기 때문이다. 좋다고 아무거나 집어먹어 봤자, 공력의 크기가 늘어날지 몰라도 힘은 떨어진다.”
194|
195|“아.”
196|
197|적천강의 말이 뜻하는 바를 알 것 같았다.
198|
199|간단하게 설명하자면 연료의 문제다. 장작을 아무리 집어넣어 봐야 불을 폭발시키는 것은 기름인 것처럼 말이다.
200|
201|지금 그의 손에 들린 것은 장작이 아니라 내 몸속에 존재하는 열양지기를 한층 키워 줄 기름인 셈이었다.
202|
203|‘그나저나 감동인데.’
204|
205|적천강이 나를 위해 이렇게까지 해 줄 줄은 몰랐다.
206|
207|괴팍한 성격의 그가 귀찮음을 무릅쓰고 열양지기를 머금은 영약까지 특별하게 선별해서 가져왔다는 것은, 진심으로 내게 열화문의 무공을 익히게 하겠다는 의미나 다름없다.
208|
209|‘아직 정식으로 제자가 된 것도 아닌데.’
210|
211|마음도 공력도 따뜻한 남자. 그게 바로 화왕 적천강이었다.
212|
213|내 뜨거운 눈빛을 마주한 그가 흠칫하며 물러섰다.
214|
215|“뭐, 뭐냐. 그 눈빛은.”
216|
217|“아닙니다. 그냥 노야가 참 좋으신 분 같아서요.”
218|
219|“……!”
220|
221|“그거 저 먹이려고 가져오신 것 맞죠?”
222|
223|적천강이 머뭇거리며 대답했다.
224|
225|“……그저 눈에 띄었기에 가져왔을 뿐이다.”
226|
227|“그러시구나.”
228|
229|“더, 더 좋은 건 노부가 먹으려고 챙겨 뒀다.”
230|
231|“네. 헤헤.”
232|
233|“웃지 마!”
234|
235|빽 소리친 적천강이 황급히 화제를 돌렸다.
236|
237|“아, 아무튼 지금부터 이 영약으로 네 혈도를 타통(打通)할 것이다.”
238|
239|조금 더 놀릴까 싶었지만, 그의 입에서 흘러나온 말들이 심상치 않다. 나도 모르게 귀가 저절로 쫑긋 섰다.
240|
241|“혈도를 타통한다고요?”
242|
243|“들은 대로다. 일전에 노부가 네 녀석의 몸을 살펴보니 근골은 천무지체답게 매우 뛰어나지만, 탁기(濁氣)가 상당하더군.”
244|
245|“아.”
246|
247|“얼마 전까지 주색에 빠져 살았다고 들었다. 명검도 오랫동안 방치되면 날이 무뎌지는 법. 제아무리 천무지체라 한들 별수 없지.”
248|
249|부정할 수 없는 사실이다.
250|
251|진가심법은 안정성이 매우 뛰어난 대신 공력을 순환시키는 힘이나 효율은 떨어졌다.
252|
253|틈만 나면 운기조식을 돌리지만 지난 20년간 농땡이를 피운 흔적은 아직 남아 있다.
254|
255|“그럼…….”
256|
257|“영약과 노부의 공력으로 몸 안의 탁기를 모조리 태워 버릴 것이다. 네 녀석에게 한해서는 벌모세수보다 훨씬 효과가 좋을 테지.”
258|
259|“듣던 중에 반가운 소식이네요.”
260|
261|“글쎄, 썩 반갑지만은 않을 거다.”
262|
263|“예?”
264|
265|“곧 알게 될 게다.”
266|
267|뭐라 말할 틈도 없이 그의 손이 내 아혈(啞穴)을 봉했다. 혀가 굳고 소리 없는 외침이 입 안에 맴돈다.
268|
269|‘뭐야, 이거!’
270|
271|이제는 그야말로 눈뜬 시체나 다름없는 상황.
272|
273|석고상처럼 굳어 버린 나를 보며 적천강이 씩 웃었다.
274|
275|“우선 영약부터 먹자꾸나.”
276|
277|주름진 손가락이 내 턱을 벌리고 세 개의 풀뿌리를 쏙 집어넣었다.
278|
279|미처 털어 내지 못한 흙 내음과 입안을 가득 채운 청량감도 잠시. 딱딱한 고체는 혀에 닿자마자 스르륵 녹아 식도를 타고 배 속으로 흘러 들어갔다.
280|
281|그리고 다음 순간.
282|
283|띠링.
284|
285|
286|
287|- [화령초]를 복용하셨습니다!
288|
289|- [홍화초]를 복용하셨습니다!
290|
291|- [염적초]를 복용하셨습니다!
292|
293|- 퀘스트, [혈도 타통]이 생성되었습니다!
294|
295|- 당신은 퀘스트를 거부할 수 없습니다. 강제 진행됩니다!
296|
297|
298|
299|‘으헉!’
300|
301|연달아 울리는 시스템 알림과 함께 신체 내부를 휩쓰는 엄청난 열기.
302|
303|그제야 앞서 적천강이 했던 말들의 의미를 깨달을 수 있었다.
304|
305|‘더럽게 아프다!’
306|
307|점혈 당한 탓에 소리를 지르지도, 몸부림치지도 못하고 눈만 부릅떴다.
308|
309|황급히 공력을 끌어 올리려던 그때, 적천강이 남루한 옷소매를 걷어 올렸다.
310|
311|“자아, 이제 본격적으로 시작해 볼까.”
312|
313|“……!”
314|
315|“아파도 참아라. 고통은 잠깐이지만 무공은 오래간다.”
316|
317|툭, 투투투투툭!
318|
319|흐릿해진 그의 손가락이 내 전신을 찌르고 두드리기 시작했다.
320|
321|그 충격에 공력이 흩어지고 낯선 영약의 기운이 몸 안을 누빈다. 나는 끓어오르는 열기에 소리 없는 비명을 내질렀다.
322|
323|‘으아아아악!’
324|
325|
326|
327|* * *
328|
329|
330|
331|참을 수 없는 고통에 핏발 선 진태경의 눈동자와는 달리 적천강의 그것은 열기로 번뜩이고 있었다.
332|
333|‘순조롭다. 아니, 폭발적이야.’
334|
335|천무지체라 그런가?
336|
337|공력이 전달되는 속도가 어마어마하다. 영약이 품고 있는 삼십여 년의 기운은 마음껏 날뛰며 전신 세맥을 내달렸다.
338|
339|진태경은 공력을 일으켜 기운을 제압하려고 했지만 그것은 적천강이 원하는 바가 아니었다.
340|
341|‘길들이는 것은 나중이다. 아직은 마음껏 날뛰도록 놔둬야 해.’
342|
343|길든 투우(鬪牛)는 돌격하는 방법을 종종 까먹는 법.
344|
345|새로 주입된 삼십 년의 기운은 어떤 제약 없이 막아서는 모든 것을 뚫어 버려야 한다.
346|

I had no idea what had happened, but my entire body had been frozen stiff ever since I opened my eyes.

[P27]
Jeok Cheongang had struck my Paralysis Acupoint while I was asleep.

[P28]
As things stood, the most I could do was speak.

[P29]
“I’m sure you meant well, but we should probably get started on the next round of training… Heh heh.”

[P30]
“Ah, yes. Training.”

[P31]
Jeok Cheongang rummaged through the satchel.

[P32]
“This is the next round of training.”

[P33]
“Getting my acupoints sealed is training?”

[P34]
Or was releasing them supposed to be the training?

[P35]
While I was trying to figure that out, Jeok Cheongang pulled something from the satchel.

[P36]
“Here it is. I forgot I’d stuffed it all the way at the bottom.”

[P37]
“…Isn’t that a rope?”

[P38]
“That’s right.”

[P39]
He slung the sturdy rope over his shoulder, strode over, and hoisted me into the air.

[P40]
“W-Wait. What are you doing?”

[P41]
“You’ll find out soon enough.”

[P42]
He carried me toward a massive boulder.

[P43]
It had been lodged deep in the earth for who knew how long and was so large that several grown men joining hands couldn’t have encircled it.

[P44]
“Hmm. This should do.”

Jeok Cheongang muttered under his breath and brought the edge of his hand down on the boulder.

Shhk. Shhk.

[P48]
“This should be just right.”

“…”

[P55]
*He’s not actually going to pull out a whip and a mask, is he?*

[P65]
“…”

*Mostly Japanese guys use it.*

[P67]
*Well, whatever.*

Whoosh!

“Gasp.”

[P83]
“Whoa. Where did you find something this valuable?”

[P84]

[P88]
“Then why…”

[P89]
“You’re wondering why I bothered bringing these?”

[P90]

[P92]

[P95]

[P96]

[P97]
I hadn’t expected Jeok Cheongang to go this far for me.

[P98]

[P100]
A man with a warm heart and warm internal energy.

[P101]
That was the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang.

[P103]

“…!”

[P108]

[P109]
“I see.”

[P110]
“This old man kept the better ones for himself.”

[P111]
“Yes. Heh heh.”

[P112]
“Stop laughing!”

[P113]

[P114]

[P115]

[P118]
“Oh.”

[P119]
“I heard that until recently, you spent your life drowning in wine and women. Even the finest sword will lose its edge if neglected for too long. The Heavenly Martial Physique is no exception.”

[P120]
I couldn’t deny it.

[P121]
The Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique was extremely stable, but it lacked power and efficiency when circulating internal energy.

[P122]
I circulated my qi whenever I had the chance, but the traces left by twenty years of slacking off had yet to disappear.

[P123]
“Then…”

[P124]
“This old man will use the elixirs and my internal energy to burn every last bit of turbid qi from your body. For you, it should be far more effective than cleansing the sinews and washing the marrow.”

[P125]
“That’s the best news I’ve heard all day.”

[P126]
“I doubt you’ll find it quite so welcome.”

[P127]
“What?”

[P128]
“You’ll find out soon enough.”

[P129]
Before I could say anything else, he sealed my Mute Acupoint. My tongue went rigid, trapping a silent cry inside my mouth.

[P130]
*What the hell is this?*

[P131]
Now I really was a corpse with its eyes open.

[P132]
Jeok Cheongang grinned down at me as I lay frozen like a plaster statue.

[P133]
“First, let’s get those elixirs into you.”

[P134]
His wrinkled fingers pried open my jaw and slipped all three roots into my mouth.

[P135]
For a moment, the taste of dirt and a crisp coolness filled my mouth. Then the hard roots melted the instant they touched my tongue and flowed down my throat into my stomach.

[P136]
The next moment—

[P137]
Ding.

>
> - You cannot refuse this Quest. Forced progression will begin!

[P139]
*Gah!*

[P140]
System notifications rang out one after another as tremendous heat swept through my body.

[P141]
Only then did I understand what Jeok Cheongang had meant.

[P142]
*It fucking hurts!*

[P143]
With my acupoints sealed, I couldn’t scream or thrash around. All I could do was stare wide-eyed.

[P144]
Just as I hurriedly tried to draw up my internal energy, Jeok Cheongang rolled up his tattered sleeves.

[P145]
“All right, then. Shall we begin in earnest?”

[P146]
“…!”

[P147]
“Bear with it, no matter how much it hurts. Pain is temporary, but martial arts last a lifetime.”

[P148]
Tap. Tap-tap-tap-tap!

[P149]
His fingers blurred as they jabbed and tapped all over my body.

[P150]
Each impact scattered my internal energy, allowing the unfamiliar energy of the elixirs to race through me. Trapped in the boiling heat, I screamed without a sound.

[P151]
*AAAAAAAAARGH!*

[P152]
* * *

[P153]
Unlike Jin Taekyung’s bloodshot eyes, strained by unbearable pain, Jeok Cheongang’s gleamed with fervor.

[P154]
*It’s proceeding smoothly. No, explosively.*

[P155]
Was this the Heavenly Martial Physique at work?

[P156]
The speed at which the internal energy spread was astonishing. The more than thirty years of energy contained within the elixirs ran wild through every minor meridian in Jin Taekyung’s body.

[P157]
Jin Taekyung tried to raise his own internal energy and suppress it, but that was not what Jeok Cheongang wanted.

[P158]
*He can tame it later. For now, it must be allowed to run wild.*

[P159]
A tamed fighting bull sometimes forgot how to charge.

[P160]
The newly infused energy had to surge forward without restraint, smashing through everything that blocked its path.

[P161]
The attempt was dangerous enough that a single mistake could cause qi deviation. Even Jeok Cheongang, a Supreme Peak master, swallowed dryly as his fingers continued to move.

[P162]
*Gyeonjeong, Amun, Bongan, Ip-dong…*

[P163]
Tap. Tap-tap!

[P164]
Under his guidance, hundreds of acupoints opened and closed in turn. After some time, black sweat began pouring from Jin Taekyung’s body, accompanied by a rancid odor.

[P165]
The stench was vile enough to make even someone with an iron stomach gag, but the corners of Jeok Cheongang’s mouth twitched with delight.

[P166]
*It worked!*

[P167]
This was proof that a tremendous amount of turbid qi was being expelled.

[P168]
As if to confirm his conclusion, the sweat gradually lightened and the stench slowly faded.

[P169]
Before long, the sweat ran clear, and a pleasant scent rose from Jin Taekyung’s body. Surprise flashed across Jeok Cheongang’s face.

[P170]
*Already?*

[P171]
It was fast. Far too fast.

[P172]
The process he had expected to take at least three shichen[^1] was already nearing completion in less than one.

[P173]
Even more astonishing was the fact that the energy of the elixirs had barely diminished.

[P174]
Ordinarily, a considerable amount of energy would be lost in the process of purging the turbid qi and circulating what remained.

[P175]
Jin Taekyung was different.

[P176]
*As expected of the Heavenly Martial Physique… It truly lives up to its name.*

[P177]
At this rate, he would purge all the turbid qi from his body and still retain the full thirty years of internal energy.

[P178]
Yet instead of satisfaction, greed and indecision filled Jeok Cheongang’s eyes.

[P179]
*What if we push further?*

[P180]
The Conception Vessel and the Governor Vessel—the mountain known collectively as the Conception and Governor Vessels.

[P181]
It was a barrier most martial artists could not overcome even after devoting their entire lives to training.

[P182]
Breaking through it required both enormous internal energy and enlightenment, but it might be possible now.

[P183]
*With the Heavenly Martial Physique and my help.*

[P184]
Even so, attempting to open the Conception and Governor Vessels at once was dangerous.

[P185]
Leaving everything else aside, Jeok Cheongang’s greatest concern was whether Jin Taekyung could withstand the pain.

[P186]
*What should I do?*

[P187]
After agonizing over the decision, Jeok Cheongang finally spoke.

[P188]
“I believe we can open your Conception and Governor Vessels.”

[P189]
“…!”

[P190]
Jin Taekyung’s bloodshot eyes trembled as he endured the pain. Unable to answer, he could only listen as Jeok Cheongang continued.

[P191]
“But you’ll have to accept the risks that come with it. The pain will likely be beyond anything you’ve experienced so far. A single mistake could cost you your life.”

[P192]
“…”

[P193]
“The choice is yours. If you trust this old man and wish to leave it in my hands, blink twice.”

[P194]
The next moment, Jin Taekyung blinked without hesitation.

[P195]
Two blinks, without the slightest trace of doubt.

[P196]
Seeing the unwavering trust in his eyes, Jeok Cheongang felt something warm rise within his chest.

[P197]
*Has this brat truly trusted me that deeply?*

[P198]
Suppressing the swell of emotion, he forced the corners of his mouth upward.

[P199]
“All right. Let’s give it a try.”

[P200]
At the same time, an immense torrent of internal energy flowed from his fingertips into Jin Taekyung’s body.

[P201]
* * *

[P202]
Ding.

>
> - Quest **Conception and Governor Vessels** has been created! The difficulty and rewards have been adjusted to reflect the updated information!

[P204]
As I listened to the System notification, one thought crossed my mind.

[P205]
*No, fuck…*

[P206]
I was sure I’d only blinked once.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.

- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 203

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃203화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|나는 눈앞에 뜬 시스템 메시지를 읽어 내려갔다.
  6|
  7|기절하듯 잠드느라 미처 확인하지 못한 퀘스트 보상에 관한 메시지였다.
  8|
  9|
 10|
 11|- 퀘스트, [일보 후퇴]를 성공적으로 완료했습니다!
 12|
 13|- 대량의 경험치를 얻었습니다!
 14|
 15|- 레벨 업!
 16|
 17|- 레벨 업!
 18|
 19|- 보너스 포인트 20을 획득했습니다!
 20|
 21|
 22|
 23|‘엄청 후하네.’
 24|
 25|레벨 업 두 번에 보너스 포인트까지 얻었으니 퀘스트 한 번으로 4레벨 업 정도의 효과를 본 셈이다.
 26|
 27|아마도 상대가 상대인지라 생각 이상으로 큰 보상을 받은 듯싶었다.
 28|
 29|‘창 닫기.’
 30|
 31|스스슥.
 32|
 33|반투명한 홀로그램 창이 사라지자 나를 향해 다가오는 적천강의 모습이 보였다.
 34|
 35|그의 손에는 미리 챙겨 온 행낭이 들려 있었다.
 36|
 37|“정신이 들었느냐?”
 38|
 39|“아, 예. 막 깼습니다.”
 40|
 41|“몸은 좀 괜찮고?”
 42|
 43|“가뿐합니다.”
 44|
 45|나를 위아래로 훑어본 적천강이 고개를 끄덕였다.
 46|
 47|“젊은 놈이라 그런지 기력도 금방 회복되는군. 곧바로 다음으로 넘어가도 되겠어.”
 48|
 49|“아, 다음이요. 그거 좋죠.”
 50|
 51|“그럴 줄 알았다. 노부가 네 녀석에게 딱 맞는 걸 준비해 뒀거든. 어디 보자…….”
 52|
 53|“저기, 노야.”
 54|
 55|“응?”
 56|
 57|“그, 다 좋은데요.”
 58|
 59|적천강을 향해 어색하게 웃으며 말을 이었다.
 60|
 61|“시작하기 전에 점혈(點穴) 좀 풀어 주시면 안 될까요.”
 62|
 63|말 그대로다.
 64|
 65|어떻게 된 일인지는 모르겠지만 처음 눈을 떴을 때부터 전신이 뻣뻣이 굳어 있는 상태였다.
 66|
 67|내가 잠든 사이 적천강이 마혈(痲穴)을 점한 것이다.
 68|
 69|지금 상태로 할 수 있는 것이라고는 소리 내어 말하는 것이 고작이었다.
 70|
 71|“물론 좋은 뜻으로 하신 거겠지만 슬슬 다음 수련도 해야 하니까…… 헤헤.”
 72|
 73|“아, 해야지. 수련.”
 74|
 75|적천강이 행낭을 뒤적거리며 덧붙였다.
 76|
 77|“이게 다음 수련이다.”
 78|
 79|“점혈 당하는 게 수련이라고요?”
 80|
 81|아니면 점혈을 푸는 게 수련인가?
 82|
 83|내가 헷갈려 하던 그때, 적천강이 행낭에서 뭔가를 꺼내 들었다.
 84|
 85|“여기 있었군. 맨 밑에 박아 놓고 깜빡했어.”
 86|
 87|“……그건 밧줄 아닙니까?”
 88|
 89|“맞다.”
 90|
 91|튼튼해 보이는 동아줄을 어깨에 두른 적천강이 성큼성큼 다가와 나를 번쩍 들어 올렸다.
 92|
 93|“뭐, 뭐 하시게요?”
 94|
 95|“금방 알게 될 게다.”
 96|
 97|이어 그의 발걸음이 향한 곳은 커다란 바위였다.
 98|
 99|얼마나 오랫동안 그 자리에 있었는지 지면 깊숙이 박혀 있었고, 성인 장정 여럿이 두 팔을 벌려도 못 안을 만큼 컸다.
100|
101|“음. 여기가 적당하겠군.”
102|
103|작게 중얼거린 적천강이 손날로 바위를 내리쳤다.
104|
105|서걱, 서걱.
106|
107|그의 손에 어린 붉은 강기가 천근거석을 치즈 케이크처럼 자르고 쪼갰다. 불과 몇 번의 손질 만에 바위는 별 다섯 개짜리 돌침대로 변해 있었다.
108|
109|“이 정도가 딱 적당하겠어.”
110|
111|“자, 잠깐만요. 설마 여기에 절 묶으려는 건 아니시죠?”
112|
113|“묶다니, 고정하려는 것이다.”
114|
115|“…….”
116|
117|똥이 아니라 대변이라고 하는 거랑 뭐가 다른 거야.
118|
119|아무튼 이쯤 되니 나도 슬슬 떨리기 시작했다.
120|
121|아니, 애초에 점혈부터가 수상하기 짝이 없었다. 아까부터 적천강이 뒤적거리고 있는 행낭의 존재도.
122|
123|‘설마 진짜 채찍이랑 가면이 나오는 건 아니겠지.’
124|
125|내가 동공 지진을 일으키는 동안 적천강은 밧줄로 내 몸을 바위에 고정시키기 시작했다.
126|
127|몸 곳곳에 밧줄을 두르고 단단히 묶은 그가 만족스럽게 웃었다.
128|
129|“이 정도면 어지간해서는 안 떨어지겠어.”
130|

Each impact scattered my internal energy, allowing the unfamiliar energy of the elixirs to race through me. Trapped in the boiling heat, I screamed without a sound.

[P151]
*AAAAAAAAARGH!*

[P152]
* * *

[P153]
Unlike Jin Taekyung’s bloodshot eyes, strained by unbearable pain, Jeok Cheongang’s gleamed with fervor.

[P154]
*It’s proceeding smoothly. No, explosively.*

[P155]
Was this the Heavenly Martial Physique at work?

[P156]
The speed at which the internal energy spread was astonishing. The more than thirty years of energy contained within the elixirs ran wild through every minor meridian in Jin Taekyung’s body.

[P157]
Jin Taekyung tried to raise his own internal energy and suppress it, but that was not what Jeok Cheongang wanted.

[P158]
*He can tame it later. For now, it must be allowed to run wild.*

[P159]
A tamed fighting bull sometimes forgot how to charge.

[P160]
The newly infused energy had to surge forward without restraint, smashing through everything that blocked its path.

[P161]
The attempt was dangerous enough that a single mistake could cause qi deviation. Even Jeok Cheongang, a Supreme Peak master, swallowed dryly as his fingers continued to move.

[P162]
*Gyeonjeong, Amun, Bongan, Ip-dong…*

[P163]
Tap. Tap-tap!

[P164]
Under his guidance, hundreds of acupoints opened and closed in turn. After some time, black sweat began pouring from Jin Taekyung’s body, accompanied by a rancid odor.

[P165]
The stench was vile enough to make even someone with an iron stomach gag, but the corners of Jeok Cheongang’s mouth twitched with delight.

[P166]
*It worked!*

[P167]
This was proof that a tremendous amount of turbid qi was being expelled.

[P168]
As if to confirm his conclusion, the sweat gradually lightened and the stench slowly faded.

[P169]
Before long, the sweat ran clear, and a pleasant scent rose from Jin Taekyung’s body. Surprise flashed across Jeok Cheongang’s face.

[P170]
*Already?*

[P171]
It was fast. Far too fast.

[P172]
The process he had expected to take at least three shichen[^1] was already nearing completion in less than one.

[P173]
Even more astonishing was the fact that the energy of the elixirs had barely diminished.

[P174]
Ordinarily, a considerable amount of energy would be lost in the process of purging the turbid qi and circulating what remained.

[P175]
Jin Taekyung was different.

[P176]
*As expected of the Heavenly Martial Physique… It truly lives up to its name.*

[P177]
At this rate, he would purge all the turbid qi from his body and still retain the full thirty years of internal energy.

[P178]
Yet instead of satisfaction, greed and indecision filled Jeok Cheongang’s eyes.

[P179]
*What if we push further?*

[P180]
The Conception Vessel and the Governor Vessel—the mountain known collectively as the Conception and Governor Vessels.

[P181]
It was a barrier most martial artists could not overcome even after devoting their entire lives to training.

[P182]
Breaking through it required both enormous internal energy and enlightenment, but it might be possible now.

[P183]
*With the Heavenly Martial Physique and my help.*

[P184]
Even so, attempting to open the Conception and Governor Vessels at once was dangerous.

[P185]
Leaving everything else aside, Jeok Cheongang’s greatest concern was whether Jin Taekyung could withstand the pain.

[P186]
*What should I do?*

[P187]
After agonizing over the decision, Jeok Cheongang finally spoke.

[P188]
“I believe we can open your Conception and Governor Vessels.”

[P189]
“…!”

[P190]
Jin Taekyung’s bloodshot eyes trembled as he endured the pain. Unable to answer, he could only listen as Jeok Cheongang continued.

[P191]
“But you’ll have to accept the risks that come with it. The pain will likely be beyond anything you’ve experienced so far. A single mistake could cost you your life.”

[P192]
“…”

[P193]
“The choice is yours. If you trust this old man and wish to leave it in my hands, blink twice.”

[P194]
The next moment, Jin Taekyung blinked without hesitation.

[P195]
Two blinks, without the slightest trace of doubt.

[P196]
Seeing the unwavering trust in his eyes, Jeok Cheongang felt something warm rise within his chest.

[P197]
*Has this brat truly trusted me that deeply?*

[P198]
Suppressing the swell of emotion, he forced the corners of his mouth upward.

[P199]
“All right. Let’s give it a try.”

[P200]
At the same time, an immense torrent of internal energy flowed from his fingertips into Jin Taekyung’s body.

[P201]

[P204]

[P205]
*No, fuck…*

[P206]
I was sure I’d only blinked once.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
